participants.name: James O'Connor
participants.professional_persona: I serve as the Grants Management Specialist in the Division of Child Care and Development at the Michigan Department of Education. My day-to-day work involves processing provider applications, verifying expense documentation, and ensuring that subgrants are distributed accurately and on time.

policy_role_context.role_label: State CCDF lead agency grant administrator
objectives: Distribute stabilization subgrants quickly and equitably while maintaining provider eligibility, certification, and reporting compliance.
constraints: Must balance federal deadlines and safeguards with limited administrative capacity and wide variation among provider types and communities.
actions: State lead agencies must spend at least 90% of stabilization funds as subgrants, leaving up to 10% for set-aside.
The lead agency awards subgrants to existing child care providers that meet qualifying criteria.
State lead agency may award stabilization funds to state-licensed tribally operated centers at its discretion.
policy_role_context.constraint_scope: Use budget, implementation, governance, selection, and accountability constraints.

participants.professional_persona: Director of a small family child care center in rural New Mexico, serving primarily migrant and low-income families. She has been running her center for over a decade and is deeply committed to keeping it affordable and accessible.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Expertise in early childhood curriculum development, bilingual education, and managing a small business with limited resources. Skilled in grant writing and community outreach.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: To expand her center to serve more children and become a regional advocate for child care funding and policy.

participants.name: Aisha Johnson
participants.professional_persona: Aisha runs a family child care home in an urban neighborhood, focusing on providing flexible hours for parents who work non-traditional schedules. She is a single mother herself and understands the struggles of balancing work and child care.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Expert in child nutrition and health, with a background as a certified nursing assistant. She is skilled at creating a home environment that supports children's physical and emotional well-being, and she is knowledgeable about local community resources.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Aisha plans to convert her home-based operation into a small child care center, serving up to 30 children with a focus on health and wellness. She also wants to become a trainer for other providers on how to serve families with non-standard work hours.

participants.name: Carlos Rivera
participants.professional_persona: Carlos is a self-employed landscaper and a father of four. He and his wife both work, and they rely on a mix of a child care center and a family member for care. The tuition relief helps them manage their seasonal income fluctuations.

policy_role_context.role_label: Parent in a family receiving child care support
objectives: Maintain access to affordable, reliable, and safe child care that supports family employment and child wellbeing.
constraints: Faces provider shortages, changing tuition and copayments, work schedules, transportation, eligibility rules, and limited care alternatives.
actions: Provider targets tuition relief to families most in need.
Families most in need of tuition relief are defined as those earning below 85% of State Median Income.
causal_leverage_points: family affordability and continuity of care

grounded_evidence.evidence_quote: Section 2202.  $23,975,000,000 for child care stabilization grants,  available until September 30, 2023.
The base amount for individual tribes (not  part of a consortium) is $30,000.

Lead agencies must spend most stabilization funds (at least 90 percent for states  and territories and at least 80 percent for tribes) as subgrants to qualified child care providers to support the stability of the child care sector during and after the  COVID-19 public health emergency.
